hints: Look carefully at each photomicrograph and name the mitotic stage. Are any of these cells already split into two separate daughter cells?
Remember when DNA doubles and when it halves. DNA is copied in S phase of interphase, so what is the DNA content from prophase right through to telophase, before cytokinesis happens?
walkthrough:
**Identify what stage each cell is in**

First, let's read the pictures like a biologist. Cell 1 has chromosomes lined up in the middle, so this is metaphase. Cell 3 has long, tangled condensing chromosomes, so this is prophase. Cell 4 has chromatids pulled apart toward opposite poles, so this is anaphase. Cell 2 has two groups at opposite poles but no dividing wall yet, so this is telophase before cytokinesis.

All four are still single cells in mitosis.

**Recall how DNA amount changes in the cell cycle**

Think of a cell after cytokinesis as your baseline. It is in early G1 with the normal amount of DNA, let's call it 2n chromosomes and 2 DNA molecules per diploid set.

In S phase, every DNA molecule is replicated:
$$DNA \ after \ S = 2 \times DNA \ after \ cytokinesis$$
That doubled amount stays in the one cell all through prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. It is only halved again when cytokinesis splits one cell into two.

**Apply this to cells 1 to 4**

Cells 1, 3 and 4 are clearly before the split, so they must contain the doubled DNA. The tricky one is cell 2. Even though you can see two chromosome groups, the cytoplasm has not divided yet. It is still counted as one cell containing twice the DNA.

So 1, 2, 3 and 4 all contain twice as many DNA molecules as after cytokinesis.

options.A: Correct. All four images show a single cell after S phase but before cytokinesis, so each contains the replicated (doubled) DNA content.
options.B: Incorrect. This wrongly leaves out cell 3. Prophase follows S phase, so DNA has already doubled.
options.C: Incorrect. This wrongly leaves out cells 2 and 4. Anaphase and telophase cells before cytokinesis still hold both sets of chromatids in one cell.
options.D: Incorrect. This wrongly leaves out cells 1 and 3. Prophase and metaphase cells already have replicated chromosomes with two chromatids each.
